description: Rock ages, faults and seismic hazard (experiment E16).

hazard._note: decay length, reference velocity, zone weight and class thresholds searched on the Earth test (earth_hazard_validation.py --grid; best 0.87 of 71 cities, leave-one-out 0.85); boundary weights fixed by class

periods._source: International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2023/09 (ICS); Precambrian by eon and era

age._note: Rock formation ages (E16). Sediments are sampled from a power law, area density ~ age^-a (Wilkinson et al. 2009, a = 0.86), between the limits of their setting; crystalline rocks take the age of their province's last tectonic event (history E07).

faults._note: Faults: plate contacts (classes of Bird 2003) and the contacts of tectonic provinces on continental crust; activity from the age of the event that made or last moved them.
faults._velocity_note: length-weighted medians of the PB2002 steps per class; used for world boundaries whose rate the scenario does not give (trenches, transforms). Ridges use their spreading rate (history.json).
faults._activity_note: plate contacts are active; faults of rifted margins went dormant when spreading began; continental rifts (1-15 Ma) are active; other contacts by the age of their event: <= 30 Ma active, <= 66 Ma dormant, older inactive. Contacts of canon features dated < 1 Ma (post-glacial wetland and drowned land bridge) are not faults.

shear_zones.note: accreted arc terrane with pervasive shear zones, as the Lachlan orogen of Victoria (CONSTRAINTS decision 13)
